title: DUALFORMER: CONTROLLABLE FAST AND SLOW THINKING BY LEARNING WITH RANDOMIZED REASONING TRACES
abstract: Dualformer is a single Transformer model that seamlessly integrates both fast and slow reasoning modes by training on randomized reasoning traces. It outperforms baselines in both performance and computational efficiency across all three modes.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're navigating a maze. You can either think fast and make quick decisions or think slow and deliberate on each step. Dualformer is a model that can do both, just like humans. It's trained on randomized reasoning traces to achieve this.

This allows it to be more efficient and accurate in its decision-making.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
Dualformer is trained on data with randomized reasoning traces. This means that different parts of the traces are strategically dropped during training. At inference time, it can be configured to execute in either fast or slow mode.

This is achieved by using a simple control mechanism, where a control token is appended to the input prompt.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
Dualformer achieves state-of-the-art results in both fast and slow modes. In the fast mode, it achieves an 80% optimal rate, outperforming the Solution-Only model. In the slow mode, it achieves a 97.6% optimal rate, surpassing the Complete-Trace model.

These results demonstrate the effectiveness of Dualformer in both modes.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Dualformer's ability to integrate both fast and slow thinking modes has significant implications. It can be used in a variety of applications, from reasoning and planning to natural language processing.

The model's efficiency and accuracy make it a valuable tool for many tasks.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Dualformer's key innovation is its use of randomized reasoning traces during training. This allows the model to learn both fast and slow thinking modes.

The model's simple control mechanism also makes it easy to configure for different tasks.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
Dualformer's code is open-sourced and available on GitHub. You can try it out on your own tasks and see the benefits of fast and slow thinking.

Experiment with different control mechanisms and see how they affect the model's performance.
